Go EnvironmentManager tracks provisioned Noise environments across registration with pending/ready/failed states (Rust f5345f1ee8, #37147): RegisterDeferredNoiseEnvironment returns a registration handle whose Ready completion publishes capability roots and whose failure or abandonment is terminal; MaterializePendingNoiseEnvironment and ReportProvisioningStatus keep the same record from Pending through Ready or Failed (report-before-materialization creates it), reports are idempotent while Ready<->Failed transitions are rejected, ordinary environments ignore reports and conflict with materialization (ProvisioningModeConflict), and Status/Info defer connection until provisioning succeeds (Status returns pending without dialing; ready then dials; failed surfaces the first error).

items.reason: L2 record-replay facility (recordreplay): parses the Rust-recorded tui/tests/fixtures/oss-story.jsonl trace (8041 events) into a normalized contract view (timestamps, machine paths and model text excluded per documented rules), freezes a structural digest as a Go golden so upstream recording drift is flagged, and replays the recording's task lifecycle through Go's paginated rollout.Recorder, cross-checking persisted event sequence, item states and recoverability (Resume) against the recording; token-free and reusable in CI.

Shared-fixture double-run over the Rust apply-patch scenario corpus (25 scenarios) surfaced four real divergences that are now fixed and frozen: (1) parser whitespace leniency around patch markers (scenarios 017/018/020) now mirrors Rust's trim/trim_end marker matching including StreamingPatchParser::finish full-trim of the final line; (2) the CLI now applies hunks sequentially and keeps partial success on failure (scenario 015) like Rust's apply_patch_with_mode, while the app-server tool keeps the verify-first flow matching Rust's verify_apply_patch_args. All 25 scenarios byte-match the Rust expected trees; unit tests pin each fixed behavior.

New jsonschema package mirrors Rust's tool-input-schema policy (tools/src/json_schema.rs): sanitize (boolean coercion, const->enum, type inference, default children), prune unreachable $defs/definitions transitively (URL-decoded local refs), drop non-subset fields (pattern/format/title/minimum/...), and compact oversized schemas (5KB budget, depth 3, four lossy passes). The parity verifier feeds the six committed Rust json_schema_policy fixtures through Go and passes every preserved/pruned/dropped assertion plus the oversized compaction assertions. Wired into mcp.ToolExecutor.Spec so the model-visible parameters of MCP tools match Rust's mcp_tool_to_responses_api_tool.

Extended the tool input-schema policy to the remaining imported-tool surfaces: (1) dynamic tools now normalize through jsonschema in dynamicToolInputSchema, mirroring Rust parse_dynamic_tool; (2) Agent Plugin v1 MCP tools get Rust's MAX_SERIALIZED_MCP_TOOL_BYTES (8000) fallback - when the normalized schema still exceeds the cap the parameters degrade to {type:object, additionalProperties:true}, mirroring agent_plugin_mcp_tool_to_responses_api_tool; the AgentPlugin flag is threaded from MCPServerStatus.PluginID through RuntimeToolInfo/ToolExecutorOptions. Unit tests pin both wirings.

New verifier diffs Go's recognized top-level config keys against Rust core/config.schema.json (94 properties): 13 genuinely-supported keys (auto_review, check_for_update_on_startup, default_permissions, goals, memories, orchestrator, permissions, plan_mode_reasoning_effort, plugins, projects, responses_api_metadata, skills, tool_suggest) were missing from knownTopLevelConfigFields and are now recognized (strict validation no longer rejects them); 16 Rust-only unsupported properties and 6 Go extensions/legacy keys are explicitly allowlisted with auditable reasons. config.KnownTopLevelConfigFields() is exported for the diff.

Method-5 differential harness: a seeded corpus of random patches/workspaces is applied by the Rust apply_patch release binary (oracle, built from the frozen 9ded177ce checkout) and Go's apply_patch CLI, requiring identical exit status and byte-identical final trees. 3000+ cases across two seeds pass. The harness immediately surfaced a real divergence: Go accepted update+move hunks with zero change lines (pure moves) while Rust rejects them per the spec (change+ required); parseUpdate now requires at least one chunk, and the old TestApplyPureMovePreservesContent was replaced by TestUpdateMoveRequiresChangeLinesLikeRust pinning the Rust behavior. Skips when the oracle binary is absent.

The seeded differential corpus now also covers unicode content lines, CRLF workspaces, paths with spaces, add-overwrite of existing files, duplicate targets, *** Environment ID headers, *** End of File markers, context lines and multiple @@ chunks per update; 8000+ cases across four seeds match the Rust oracle with no further divergences.

Shared-fixture double-run over backend-client/tests/fixtures: Go chatgptapi.CodeTaskDetailsResponse extracts the same unified diff (current_diff_task_turn preferred, pr output_diff fallback), assistant text messages, joined user prompt and combined error message as the Rust types.rs tests assert, from the same committed fixtures.

Method-5 property test for rollout writing: random turn/item operation sequences written by the paginated Recorder must produce a Rust-compatible rollout - contiguous ordinals, session_meta first line, canonical event_msg payload types (task_started/item_started/item_completed/task_complete), exact item byte round-trip, item lifecycle pairing, and appendability after Resume. 120+ sequences in CI (4 seeds x 30) plus 450 high-intensity sequences verified.

The differential harness surfaced a CLI stdout divergence: Rust print_summary groups all added, then modified, then deleted, each in hunk application order, while Go's Summary() path-sorted within each kind (e.g. 'M nested/a.txt M b.txt' vs 'M b.txt M nested/a.txt'). Summary() now mirrors Rust's grouping/order; the harness compares stdout byte-exact on success and failure (both print nothing to stdout on failure) across 3500+ additional seeded cases. New TestContractVerifiersExistInGoTestFiles audits that every contract verifier name maps to a real test function in the Go tree (location-agnostic; goPaths remain implementation paths).

Completed two L0 enum-inventory items: (1) TestRustProcessSandboxTypeSurfaceAgainstGo pins the exec-server ProcessSandboxType wire values (camelCase none/macosSeatbelt/linuxSeccomp/windowsRestrictedToken) against Go's execserver constants - exact match; (2) TestRustEventMsgWireNamesCoverRecordedSurface extracts the app-server EventMsg wire names (snake_case + serde renames) from protocol.rs and pins every codex_event msg.type in the oss-story recording to a current wire name or a documented historical rename (agent_message_delta -> agent_message_content_delta, agent_reasoning_raw_content_delta -> reasoning_raw_content_delta), so future event renames break the check.

TestRustErrorCodeSurfaceAgainstGo pins every wire value of the app-server v2 CodexErrorInfo and ConfigWriteErrorCode enums to Go production code (non-test files): all 17 CodexErrorInfo codes are emitted or allowlisted, all 7 ConfigWriteErrorCode codes are covered by config/api.go constants (configRequirementReadonly added to complete the surface). Two emission gaps are documented with auditable reasons: sessionBudgetExceeded (Go rollout-budget path does not surface the codexErrorInfo yet) and threadRollbackFailed (Go thread/rollback failure returns generic RPC errors); both stay monitored by the verifier and shrink as Go wires them.

TestRustModelInfoFieldSurfaceAgainstGo pins the wire fields of Rust's openai_models::ModelInfo (41 fields, excluding the serde-skipped internal marker) against Go's ModelInfo JSON surface (38 fields): 6 Rust-only fields are allowlisted with auditable reasons (availability_nux lives on Go's ModelSummary; supports_reasoning_summary_parameter is Go's supports_reasoning_summaries naming variant; apply_patch_tool_type/comp_hash/experimental_supported_tools/shell_type not yet carried), and 3 Go-only fields are documented extensions. All four L0 enum-inventory items (sandbox types, event names, error codes, model metadata) are now pinned.

Closed both monitored error-code emission gaps: (1) threadRollbackFailed - rollback request validation failures (num_turns<1, active turn) now surface a -32600 invalid-request RPC error carrying codexErrorInfo=threadRollbackFailed, mirroring Rust's core/session/handlers.rs + bespoke_event_handling.rs (invalid_request); (2) sessionBudgetExceeded - implemented the rollout budget feature end to end: config/rollout_budget.go resolves features.rollout_budget with Rust's exact validation (required limit_tokens/reminder_at_remaining_tokens, positivity bounds, finite weights defaulting to 1.0), RuntimeRouter.rolloutBudgetForSession lazily configures a shared runtimeutil.Budget per session, runTurnRuntime charges each completed turn's usage and fails the turn with ErrSessionBudgetExceeded, and the turn error mapper surfaces the sessionBudgetExceeded codexErrorInfo. TestRustErrorCodeSurfaceAgainstGo now passes with zero emission gaps (all 17 CodexErrorInfo + 7 ConfigWriteErrorCode values present in Go production code).
